custom.eventDescription: Here are some questions about eligibility and qualifying education.

item.label: What is the supplement and who can receive it?

custom.eventDescription:
The disability supplement (handicaptillæg) is an additional grant paid with ordinary SU or a final loan. It is for students whose permanent physical or mental impairment causes very significant limitations in their ability to take paid work alongside study.

You must meet the ordinary SU or final-loan conditions, attend a qualifying programme, and meet the impairment and work-capacity conditions. The authority makes an individual assessment; this chatbot cannot decide whether you qualify.

The scheme covers qualifying higher education programmes and Danish vocational education programmes (EUD), including qualifying EUX programmes. It does not cover general upper-secondary programmes, VUC, or vocational programmes outside Denmark that are not offered under Danish vocational-education legislation.

You must also meet the ordinary conditions for SU or a final loan.

No. A diagnosis does not itself establish entitlement, and there is no list of diagnoses that automatically qualify. The authority considers permanence, severity, current functioning, treatment and prognosis, and how the impairment affects the ability to take paid work. People with the same diagnosis may be affected differently.
Here are some questions about impairment and ability to work.

item.label: What about temporary illness or ongoing treatment?
How do 5–6 hours of work affect the assessment?

custom.eventDescription:
As a general rule, an impairment is permanent when it is not expected to become substantially better by itself or through treatment within a longer period of years.

A fixed one-year wait does not apply to a condition that is permanent or chronic by its nature. For other conditions, around one year may be an assessment guideline, not an automatic entitlement threshold.

Temporary injuries, isolated operations or illness periods, a single depressive episode, and pregnancy-related symptoms will normally not meet the permanence condition when recovery is expected within a manageable period.

If treatment is ongoing and the long-term effect is uncertain, a time-limited award may be possible when the evidence makes a permanent and sufficiently serious impairment probable. Ongoing treatment alone does not create entitlement.

The guidance says that someone who can work around 5–6 hours per week during study periods, including weekends, is as a starting point not entitled. Similar attention is given to full-time work for around 5–6 weeks during annual holidays.

These are assessment indicators, not automatic cut-offs. The authority considers duties, symptoms, accommodations, sickness absence and the other evidence as a whole.
Here are some questions about medical documentation.

item.label: What is the minimum medical documentation?
What should the medical records describe?
What is not sufficient on its own?

custom.eventDescription: For an application submitted on or after 1 July 2025, attach medical records for every impairment you want considered. The minimum is generally records from the relevant part of the health service that identify and medically document the impairment. The source may be a hospital, specialist, general practitioner or other relevant treatment provider, depending on the condition.

Useful records describe the condition, course and duration, current symptoms and their frequency and intensity, daily functioning, treatment and effect, prognosis, residual symptoms and side effects. Work information should describe hours, duties, accommodations and sickness absence. The authority may obtain additional information when necessary.
custom.purpose: Guideline sections 3.4 and 4; SU.dk assessment guidance.

custom.eventDescription:
A diagnosis name, medication list, appointment notice, referral, short certificate, or your own statement will normally not be enough on its own if it does not document the impairment, course, treatment, prognosis and functional consequences.

Your description is relevant but cannot replace required medical evidence. Meeting the minimum documentation requirement also does not mean the substantive eligibility conditions are met.
Here are some questions about applying, decisions and help.

item.label: What happens if documentation is missing?
How can I follow my case or contact the authority?

custom.eventDescription: Apply through minSU under “Apply for SU” and then “Disability supplement”. Apply for ordinary SU first. Identify every impairment you want considered, attach relevant medical records, and provide information about current and previous work, duties, accommodations and sickness absence. You should receive a receipt after submission.
custom.purpose: Guideline sections 3.5 and 4; SU.dk application FAQ.

custom.eventDescription:
For an application submitted on or after 1 July 2025, the authority can refuse to process it if the minimum medical-record requirement is not met. It then does not decide whether the substantive eligibility conditions are satisfied.

If the minimum was met but more information is needed, the authority may request additional material. If the application is refused for failing the minimum, missing records normally belong in a new application.

A time-limited award grants the supplement for a defined period rather than indefinitely. It may be used when the evidence makes a permanent and sufficiently serious impairment probable but, for example, the long-term effect of ongoing treatment cannot yet be finally established.

The decision states the period and relevant next steps. Any continuation is assessed using the information then available.

The written decision explains how to appeal and the applicable deadline. Follow the instructions in that decision, explain which part you disagree with and why, and attach relevant supporting information that was not already available.

Use the deadline and submission channel in your own decision because this chatbot does not store case-specific details or replace official appeal guidance.
custom.purpose: Guideline section 9; appeal instructions in the individual decision.

custom.eventDescription:
Use the case-status and contact options currently published on SU.dk. Keep your receipt and any reference number from minSU. If the authority asks for information, follow the instructions and deadline in that message.

Do not send sensitive medical information through an ordinary channel unless official instructions say it is secure. Contact details and processing information can change, so they are not embedded in this graph.
custom.purpose: Current SU.dk case-status and contact guidance.

custom.eventDescription: Here are some questions about payment, work and changes after approval.

item.label: When does payment begin and where can I find the current rate?
How do work and income affect an existing award?
What happens during a paid internship or after changing programme?

custom.eventDescription:
If the supplement is awarded, payment is generally connected to the application date and to months in which you receive ordinary SU or a final loan, subject to the detailed rules and the decision. It is not paid for months in which there is no SU or final loan.

Rates change. Use the current rate on SU.dk rather than relying on a fixed amount in this chatbot.
custom.purpose: Guideline sections 7.1–7.2; current SU.dk payment information.

custom.eventDescription:
Work and income can matter both when work capacity is assessed and after an award. Work before or during the case may be considered, including hours, duties, accommodations and sickness absence. The authority may obtain income and working-time information from the Danish Tax Agency.

An award does not mean every amount of work is prohibited, but work indicating greater capacity can lead to reassessment. Income also remains subject to the SU income rules.
custom.purpose: Guideline sections 3.4.4 and 8; SU.dk work and income FAQ.

custom.eventDescription:
The supplement is not paid for periods in which you do not receive SU or a final loan, which can include some paid-internship periods. Changing programme, institution or educational level may require action in minSU or a new assessment, depending on the circumstances.

Report relevant changes and check current SU.dk instructions or contact the authority because the result depends on the type of change and your SU status.
custom.purpose: Guideline sections 7–8; SU.dk internship and programme-change FAQ.
